transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The White House has named a new cybersecurity chief.
This comes after a week of computer crashes and online problems
in both government and high-profile companies.
NPR's Greg Myry has the details.
The new cybersecurity director at the White House will be Kirsten Davies.
She's been serving as chief information officer at the Defense Department.
Her appointment comes after a router installation went awry last week,
leading the FAA to suspend all flights from taking off nationwide.
In addition, Microsoft's email system crashed,
Apple users were unable to use popular services,
and an internal communications network went down at the National Security Agency.
The Trump administration says there's no evidence of hacking,
rather AI tools are detecting previously unknown software flaws.
As organizations race to patch or upgrade systems,
this is sometimes resulting in temporary breakdowns.
Greg Myry, NPR News, Washington.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has served computer chipmaker NVIDIA
with an investigative subpoena.
The subpoena follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Wong
after an affair with a woman who may have spied for China,
and Pierre's John Ruich has more.
The California AG's office says in a statement it's asking NVIDIA
whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China,
and whether NVIDIA misled investors and the public.
Bonta says the conduct of the company and former CEO Jensen Wong raises red flags.
Wong stepped down last week after admitting to an extramarital affair.
U.S. intelligence services believe one of the women had ties to a Chinese spy agency.
Wong had been a vocal opponent of U.S. export controls
that banned certain high-end chips from being exported to China.
John Ruich, NPR News.
The Senate has passed legislation that's designed to make changes
to permitting in the energy sector.
As NPR's Julia Simon tells us,
some Democratic lawmakers and environmentalists oppose the legislation.
Proponents of the bill say that the current permitting process is outdated,
inefficient, and needs updates.
That is, easing of environmental regulations
and changes to laws around building electrical transmission lines.
Some climate change advocates say the bill will allow the country
to build more solar, wind, and battery projects.
And many climate scientists do agree that the U.S. needs to speed up building
renewable energy projects and transmission lines.
But other Democratic lawmakers oppose the bill.
They argue it will worsen climate pollution by also making it easier
to greenlight oil and gas projects and energy-hungry data centers.
And they say it will weaken protections for clean air and water.
Julia Simon, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee in the next Congress
is investigating how Homeland Security and Justice Department officials
preserve communications when they're doing official business.
Maryland Democratic Congressman Jamie Raskin has sent letters warning he is concerned
the Trump administration is using apps that self-delete after a certain period of time.
He says that would violate laws about governmental record-keeping.
He is demanding that the agencies take steps to recover any deletions.
An original handwritten draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech
is on public display in Atlanta before it is sold at auction.
NPR's Debbie Elliott reports.
The seven-page draft is written longhand on yellow legal paper
with sections scratched through and reworked.
It's on display through Sunday at the Center for Civil and Human Rights in Atlanta,
CEO Jill Savitt says it's a foundational artifact.
Nothing has given me chills like this handwritten document
where you see him crafting one of the most iconic speeches in U.S. history
and the idea that this was a human being, a man who sat down with a pen and a piece of paper,
struggling to find the right words.
The draft was discovered in a desk drawer by civil rights activist Zernona Clayton
whose late husband was one of King's speechwriters.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Atlanta.
You're listening to NPR.
This message comes from Lisa and their lineup of beautifully crafted mattresses

California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenas NVIDIA over CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and China ties
Senate passes energy permitting bill, drawing opposition from Democrats and environmentalists
Rep. Jamie Raskin probes whether Homeland Security and Justice officials use self-deleting messaging apps
